page: Microsoft Azure FX96-24ms_v2 is an x86_64 server profile designed for memory-intensive tasks requiring high clock frequencies. Virtualized under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 24 dedicated vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The hardware architecture incorporates a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and instruction support spanning AVX-512, AMX-Tile, AMX-INT8, and cryptographic accelerators. The instance features no bundled local ephemeral storage and includes zero GPUs, requiring remote premium storage attachments for data persistence.

Memory density is the defining characteristic of this configuration, offering 1,832 GB of system RAM, which calculates to 76.33 GB per vCPU. Synthetic memory evaluation confirms strong data transfer rates, registering large-block uncached read speeds of 187.06 GB/sec and write throughput of 118.92 GB/sec. Cached small-block operations achieve 2,070.15 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput memory exchange for data-heavy pipelines.

Compute benchmarks highlight top-decile execution speed on latency-sensitive single-threaded workloads. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2,366 and a text processing score of 2,974, placing both metrics in the top 10 percent. Multithreaded execution delivered a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,770 and a PassMark CPU score of 41,641.31. Single-threaded gzip compression sustained 34.65 GB/sec, while in-memory Redis transactions recorded 38.78 million operations per second.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the FX96-24ms_v2 provides substantial cost benefits for software licensed on a per-core basis, such as commercial relational database management systems. Allocating an exceptionally high memory capacity across a constrained 24-vCPU footprint reduces software licensing requirements while keeping datasets fully resident in RAM. The instance is suited for enterprise in-memory databases, massive distributed caching tiers, and memory-constrained analytical processing.
